preamble.plain: The People of the State of New York, grateful to Almighty God for their Freedom, establish this Constitution in order to secure its blessings.

a1-s1.plain: No member of the state shall be disfranchised or deprived of the rights or privileges secured to citizens, unless by the law of the land or the judgment of peers. The legislature may provide that no primary election is held when there is no contest.
rights: the rights or privileges secured to any citizen thereof
powers: the legislature may provide that there shall be no primary election held
limits: No member of this state shall be disfranchised

a1-s2.plain: Trial by jury where guaranteed by constitutional provision shall remain inviolate forever. Parties may waive a jury in civil cases, and the legislature may allow civil verdicts by five-sixths of the jury. A defendant may waive a jury in criminal cases not punishable by death, by a written instrument signed in open court with a judge's approval.
rights: Trial by jury in all cases in which it has heretofore been guaranteed by constitutional provision shall remain inviolate forever
powers: a jury trial may be waived by the parties in all civil cases
a verdict may be rendered by not less than five-sixths of the jury in any civil case
A jury trial may be waived by the defendant in all criminal cases
The legislature may enact laws, not inconsistent herewith, governing the form, content, manner and time of presentation of the instrument effectuating such waiver

a1-s3.plain: The free exercise and enjoyment of religious profession and worship, without discrimination or preference, shall forever be allowed to all humankind, and no person shall be made incompetent as a witness for religious opinions. This liberty does not excuse licentiousness or practices inconsistent with the state's peace or safety.
rights: The free exercise and enjoyment of religious profession and worship, without discrimination or preference
limits: no person shall be rendered incompetent to be a witness on account of his or her opinions on matters of religious belief
shall not be so construed as to excuse acts of licentiousness, or justify practices inconsistent with the peace or safety of this state

a1-s4.plain: The privilege of a writ or order of habeas corpus shall not be suspended, unless the public safety requires it in case of rebellion or invasion.
rights: The privilege of a writ or order of habeas corpus
limits: shall not be suspended

a1-s5.plain: Excessive bail shall not be required, excessive fines shall not be imposed, cruel and unusual punishments shall not be inflicted, and witnesses shall not be unreasonably detained.
limits: Excessive bail shall not be required
nor excessive fines imposed
nor shall cruel and unusual punishments be inflicted
nor shall witnesses be unreasonably detained

a1-s6.plain: No person shall answer for a capital or otherwise infamous crime without grand jury indictment, except listed cases or a written waiver. The accused may defend with counsel, be informed of the accusation and confront witnesses. Double jeopardy and compelled self-incrimination are barred, officers refusing to waive immunity are disqualified, and due process is guaranteed.
rights: to appear and defend in person and with counsel
be informed of the nature and cause of the accusation
be confronted with the witnesses against him or her
powers: may waive indictment by a grand jury
The power of grand juries to inquire into the wilful misconduct in office of public officers
limits: No person shall be held to answer for a capital or otherwise infamous crime
No person shall be subject to be twice put in jeopardy for the same offense
nor shall he or she be compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against himself or herself
shall never be suspended or impaired by law
No person shall be deprived of life, liberty or property without due process of law

a1-s7.plain: Private property shall not be taken for public use without just compensation. Private roads may be opened by law after a jury of freeholders determines need and damages, paid by the person benefited. Draining swamp or agricultural lands is a public use, and general laws may permit drains on others' lands with just compensation.
powers: Private roads may be opened in the manner to be prescribed by law

general laws may be passed permitting the owners or occupants of swamp or agricultural lands to construct and maintain for the drainage thereof, necessary drains, ditches and dykes upon the lands of others
limits: Private property shall not be taken for public use without just compensation
no special laws shall be enacted for such purposes

a1-s8.plain: Every citizen may freely speak, write and publish sentiments on all subjects, being responsible for abuse of that right; no law shall restrain or abridge liberty of speech or press. In libel prosecutions truth may be given in evidence, true matter published with good motives and for justifiable ends requires acquittal, and the jury determines law and fact.
rights: may freely speak, write and publish his or her sentiments on all subjects
the truth may be given in evidence to the jury
the jury shall have the right to determine the law and the fact
limits: no law shall be passed to restrain or abridge the liberty of speech or of the press

a1-s9.plain: No law shall abridge the people's right peaceably to assemble and petition, and divorce requires due judicial proceedings. Gambling is barred except state lotteries for education, pari-mutuel horse betting and casinos at up to seven facilities. Municipalities may by vote authorize bingo, lotto and similar games run by bona fide non-profit organizations, under listed restrictions.
rights: the rights of the people peaceably to assemble and to petition the government, or any department thereof
powers: any city, town or village within the state may by an approving vote of the majority of the qualified electors
limits: No law shall be passed abridging
nor shall any divorce be granted otherwise than by due judicial proceedings
no lottery or the sale of lottery tickets, pool-selling, book-making, or any other kind of gambling
no person except a bona fide member of any such organization shall participate in the management or operation of such game
no person shall receive any remuneration for participating in the management or operation of any such game
no single prize shall exceed two hundred fifty dollars
no municipality shall have the power to pass local laws or ordinances relating to such games

a1-s11.plain: No person shall be denied the equal protection of the laws, or be subjected to discrimination in civil rights by any person, firm, corporation, institution or the state because of the listed characteristics. This does not invalidate laws designed to prevent or dismantle such discrimination.
rights: the equal protection of the laws of this state or any subdivision thereof
limits: No person shall be denied
be subjected to any discrimination in their civil rights

a1-s12.plain: The people's right to be secure against unreasonable searches and seizures, and against unreasonable interception of telephone and telegraph communications, shall not be violated. Warrants require probable cause on oath and particular descriptions; interception orders require oath of reasonable ground to believe evidence of crime may be obtained.
rights: The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures
The right of the people to be secure against unreasonable interception of telephone and telegraph communications
limits: shall not be violated
no warrants shall issue, but upon probable cause
ex parte orders or warrants shall issue only upon oath or affirmation

a1-s14.plain: Parts of the common law and colonial acts that formed the law of the colony on April 19, 1775, colonial congress and convention resolutions in force on April 20, 1777, and acts of the legislature now in force continue as state law, subject to legislative alteration. Parts repugnant to this constitution are abrogated.
powers: subject to such alterations as the legislature shall make concerning the same
limits: are hereby abrogated

a1-s16.plain: The existing right of action to recover damages for injuries resulting in death shall never be abrogated, and the amount recoverable shall not be subject to any statutory limitation.
rights: The right of action now existing to recover damages for injuries resulting in death
limits: shall never be abrogated
shall not be subject to any statutory limitation

a1-s17.plain: Labor of human beings is not a commodity or article of commerce. Laborers on public work for contractors may not work more than eight hours a day or five days a week, except in extraordinary emergency, nor be paid less than prevailing wages. Employees have the right to organize and bargain collectively.
rights: the right to organize and to bargain collectively through representatives of their own choosing
limits: is not a commodity nor an article of commerce
shall never be so considered or construed
shall be permitted to work more than eight hours in any day or more than five days in any week
nor shall he or she be paid less than the rate of wages prevailing in the same trade or occupation

a1-s18.plain: Nothing in the constitution limits the legislature's power to enact laws protecting employees' lives, health or safety, or for compensation for employee injuries or death without regard to fault, except willful intention or sole intoxication. Such compensation may be exclusive and capped for death; employer payments are a proper business cost.
powers: the power of the legislature to enact laws for the protection of the lives, health, or safety of employees
of compensation for injuries to employees or for death of employees resulting from such injuries without regard to fault as a cause thereof

a1-s19.plain: Each person shall have a right to clean air and water, and a healthful environment.
rights: a right to clean air and water, and a healthful environment

a2-s1.plain: Every citizen eighteen or over who has resided in the state, and in the county, city or village, for thirty days before an election shall be entitled to vote for all officers elected by the people and on all questions submitted to the people.
rights: shall be entitled to vote at every election for all officers elected by the people and upon all questions submitted to the vote of the people

a2-s2.plain: The legislature may, by general law, provide how, when and where qualified voters absent from their county (or from New York City) or unable to appear at the polls because of illness or physical disability may vote, and for return and canvass of their votes.
powers: The legislature may, by general law, provide a manner in which, and the time and place at which

a2-s3.plain: No person who receives or pays money or any valuable thing for a vote, promises to influence a vote, or bets on the election shall vote at that election, and a challenged person must swear or affirm this. The legislature shall exclude from suffrage persons convicted of bribery or any infamous crime.
limits: shall vote at such election
excluding from the right of suffrage all persons convicted of bribery or of any infamous crime

a2-s4.plain: For the purpose of voting, no person gains or loses a residence by being present or absent while in the service of the United States, navigating the listed waters, a student, kept at an almshouse or other supported institution, or confined in a public prison.
limits: no person shall be deemed to have gained or lost a residence

a2-s5.plain: Laws shall be made to ascertain by proper proofs which citizens are entitled to vote, and for registering voters, with registration completed at least ten days before each election. Registration is not required for town and village elections unless a law expressly provides it.
limits: Such registration shall not be required for town and village elections

a2-s6.plain: The legislature may by law set up registration systems under which a voter who applies in person stays registered as long as he or she remains qualified to vote from an address within the jurisdiction of the board where registered.
powers: The legislature may provide by law for a system or systems of registration

a2-s7.plain: All elections by the citizens shall be by ballot or another method prescribed by law, keeping voting secret, except for certain town officers. The legislature shall provide for identifying voters by signature where personal registration is required, and for voters' signatures when voting in person.
powers: or by such other method as may be prescribed by law

a2-s8.plain: Laws on boards or officers that qualify voters, distribute ballots, or receive, record or count votes shall secure equal representation of the two parties with the most votes at the preceding general election. The section does not apply to town or village elections.
powers: as the legislature may direct

a2-s9.plain: Despite section one's residence requirements, the legislature may by general law let certain recent movers, and registered voters who moved to another state within a year, vote here solely for presidential electors if they cannot qualify to vote for them elsewhere.
powers: the legislature may, by general law, provide special procedures
The legislature may also, by general law, prescribe special procedures

a3-s1.plain: The legislative power of the state is vested in the senate and assembly.
powers: The legislative power of this state shall be vested in the senate and assembly

a3-s2.plain: The senate has fifty members, except as later provided, and the assembly one hundred fifty. Senators are chosen for two years (those elected in 1895 served three), and assembly members are chosen for two years.

a3-s3.plain: The senate districts described in the constitution adopted on November 6, 1894 are continued for all purposes of future reapportionments of senate districts under section four.

a3-s4.plain: Federal census figures control legislative apportionment, with state enumerations when needed. An independent commission prepares redistricting plans that the legislature votes on under set rules. Districts must protect minority voting rights, be nearly equal, contiguous and compact, and not favor incumbents; public hearings are required.
rights: racial or minority language groups do not have less opportunity to participate in the political process than other members of the electorate and to elect representatives of their choice
powers: The legislature, by law, may provide in its discretion for an enumeration by state authorities of the inhabitants of the state
shall prepare a redistricting plan to establish senate, assembly, and congressional districts every ten years
limits: no block in a city inclosed by streets or public ways, shall be divided in the formation of senate districts
No county shall have more than one-third of all the senators
districts shall not be drawn to have the purpose of, nor shall they result in, the denial or abridgement of such rights
Districts shall not be drawn to discourage competition

a3-s5.plain: Assembly members are chosen by single districts and apportioned among counties by population, every county but Hamilton getting one. Local bodies divide counties into equal, compact, contiguous districts. Any citizen may seek supreme court review of an apportionment, decided within sixty days.
powers: the legislature may abolish the said county of Hamilton
shall be subject to review by the supreme court, at the suit of any citizen
limits: no county shall hereafter be erected unless its population shall entitle it to a member
No county shall have more members of assembly than a county having a greater number of inhabitants, excluding aliens

a3-s5-a.plain: For apportioning senate and assembly districts under this article, "inhabitants, excluding aliens" means the whole number of persons.

a3-s5-b.plain: A ten-member independent redistricting commission, appointed mostly by legislative leaders, is established to determine district lines. Members must be registered voters without listed recent political ties. The section sets quorum and voting rules, co-executive directors and staff, and state budget funding.
powers: an independent redistricting commission shall be established to determine the district lines for congressional and state legislative offices
shall appoint two co-executive directors
The co-executive directors shall appoint such staff as are necessary to perform the commission's duties
limits: No member shall within the last three years

a3-s6.plain: Each legislator receives a like annual salary fixed by law, weekly travel reimbursement during session, and allowances fixed by law for impeachment service and special offices. These may not be increased or diminished during the term, and no other extra compensation is paid.
rights: shall receive for his or her services a like annual salary, to be fixed by law
limits: Neither the salary of any member nor any other allowance so fixed may be increased or diminished during, and with respect to, the term for which he or she shall have been elected
nor shall he or she be paid or receive any other extra compensation

a3-s7.plain: A legislator must be a U.S. citizen, a New York resident for five years, and a district resident for twelve months before election. Legislators may not receive certain civil appointments during their term; accepting congress or other listed offices vacates the seat.
limits: No person shall serve as a member of the legislature
No member of the legislature shall, during the time for which he or she was elected, receive any civil appointment

a3-s8.plain: Elections of senators and assembly members are held on the Tuesday after the first Monday of November, unless the legislature directs otherwise.

a3-s9.plain: A majority of each house is a quorum. Each house sets its own rules, judges its members' elections, returns and qualifications, and chooses its officers; the senate chooses a temporary president and the assembly a speaker.
powers: Each house shall determine the rules of its own proceedings
be the judge of the elections, returns and qualifications of its own members
shall choose its own officers

a3-s10.plain: Each house keeps and publishes a journal, except parts requiring secrecy, and keeps its doors open unless the public welfare requires secrecy. Neither house may adjourn for more than two days without the other's consent.
limits: Neither house shall, without the consent of the other, adjourn for more than two days

a3-s11.plain: Members of the legislature may not be questioned in any other place for any speech or debate in either house.
limits: the members shall not be questioned in any other place

a3-s12.plain: Any bill may start in either house of the legislature, and a bill passed by one house may be amended by the other.
powers: Any bill may originate in either house of the legislature
all bills passed by one house may be amended by the other

a3-s13.plain: Every bill's enacting clause must read "The People of the State of New York, represented in Senate and Assembly, do enact as follows," and no law may be enacted except by bill.
limits: no law shall be enacted except by bill

a3-s14.plain: A bill must be printed and on members' desks in final form three calendar legislative days before final passage, unless the governor certifies the need for an immediate vote. Passage needs a majority of members elected to each branch; no amendment on last reading. Electronic format counts as printed.
limits: No bill shall be passed or become a law unless it shall have been printed and upon the desks of the members
nor shall any bill be passed or become a law, except by the assent of a majority of the members elected to each branch of the legislature
no amendment thereof shall be allowed

a3-s15.plain: A private or local bill passed by the legislature may not embrace more than one subject, and that subject must be expressed in the title.
limits: shall embrace more than one subject

a3-s16.plain: No act may provide that any existing law, or part of one, is made part of the act or is applicable, except by inserting it in the act.
limits: No act shall be passed which shall provide that any existing law, or any part thereof, shall be made or deemed a part of said act

a3-s17.plain: The legislature may not pass a private or local bill in the listed cases, including changing names, roads, county seats, venue, incorporating villages, juries, interest rates, elections, officers' fees, railroad tracks, exclusive privileges, tax exemptions and certain bridges.
limits: The legislature shall not pass a private or local bill

a3-s18.plain: On a petition signed by two-thirds of the members elected to each house, presented to the temporary president of the senate and the speaker, the members may convene the legislature on extraordinary occasions to act on the subjects in the petition.
powers: to convene the legislature on extraordinary occasions

a3-s19.plain: The legislature may not audit or allow private claims against the state, but may appropriate money for claims audited and allowed according to law. No claim barred by lapse of time may be paid, but a claimant under legal disability has two years after it is removed.
powers: may appropriate money to pay such claims as shall have been audited and allowed according to law
limits: The legislature shall neither audit nor allow any private claim or account against the state
No claim against the state shall be audited, allowed or paid

a3-s20.plain: Every bill appropriating public moneys or property for local or private purposes needs the assent of two-thirds of the members elected to each branch of the legislature.

a3-s21.plain: Sections 15, 16 and 17 of this article do not apply to bills recommended by commissioners or public agencies appointed to prepare revisions, consolidations or compilations of statutes. A bill amending an existing law is excepted only if it is itself so recommended.
limits: shall not be excepted from the provisions of sections 15, 16 and 17 of this article

a3-s22.plain: A tax law must distinctly state the tax and its object, and may not just refer to another law. But an income tax law may define income by reference to the laws of the United States, with exceptions or modifications.
powers: may define the income on, in respect to or by which such tax or taxes are imposed or measured, by reference to any provision of the laws of the United States
limits: it shall not be sufficient to refer to any other law to fix such tax or object

a3-s23.plain: On final passage of any act that imposes a tax, creates a debt or charge, makes an appropriation, or releases a claim of the state, the vote is by yeas and nays entered on the journals, and three-fifths of all members elected is the quorum.

a3-s24.plain: The legislature must provide by law for employing prisoners, and no prisoner may work where the work or its product is farmed out, contracted or sold to private parties, except voluntary work for nonprofit organizations; work for the state or public institutions is allowed.
powers: the legislature may provide by law that such prisoners may voluntarily perform work for nonprofit organizations
limits: no person in any such prison, penitentiary, jail or reformatory, shall be required or allowed to work

a3-s25.plain: To keep state and local government running in emergencies caused by enemy attack or disasters, the legislature has the power and immediate duty to provide for temporary succession to public offices and to adopt other necessary and proper measures.
powers: shall have the power and the immediate duty

a4-s1.plain: The executive power is vested in the governor, who serves four years; the lieutenant-governor is chosen at the same time for the same term. They are chosen jointly by a single vote every fourth year from 1938, and those with the most votes are elected.
powers: The executive power shall be vested in the governor

a4-s2.plain: Only a citizen of the United States, at least thirty years old, who has been a resident of New York for the five years before the election may be governor or lieutenant-governor.
limits: No person shall be eligible to the office of governor or lieutenant-governor

a4-s3.plain: The governor commands the state's military and naval forces, may convene the legislature or the senate on extraordinary occasions, reports to the legislature on the condition of the state, and must take care that the laws are faithfully executed. The governor receives a salary and an executive residence.
powers: The governor shall be commander-in-chief of the military and naval forces of the state
The governor shall have power to convene the legislature, or the senate only, on extraordinary occasions
limits: no subject shall be acted upon, except such as the governor may recommend for consideration

a4-s4.plain: The governor may grant reprieves, commutations and pardons after conviction for all offenses except treason and impeachment. For treason, the governor may suspend the sentence until the legislature acts. The governor must report each grant to the legislature annually.
powers: The governor shall have the power to grant reprieves, commutations and pardons after conviction
the governor shall have power to suspend the execution of the sentence

a4-s5.plain: The lieutenant-governor becomes governor if the governor is removed, dies or resigns, or if the governor-elect declines or dies, and acts as governor while the governor is impeached, absent, unable to serve, or has not taken the oath.

a4-s6.plain: The lieutenant-governor has the governor's qualifications, presides over the senate with only a casting vote, and receives a salary. It sets elections when both offices are vacant and makes the temporary president of the senate, then the speaker, act as governor; the legislature may provide for other cases.
powers: The legislature may provide for the devolution of the duty of acting as governor
limits: shall have only a casting vote therein
No election of a lieutenant-governor shall be had in any event except at the time of electing a governor

a4-s7.plain: Every bill passed by both houses goes to the governor, who signs it or returns it with objections; two-thirds of the members elected to each house can override. Unreturned bills become law after ten days unless the legislature adjourns. The governor may object to items of appropriation.
powers: the governor may object to one or more of such items while approving of the other portion of the bill
limits: No bill shall become a law after the final adjournment of the legislature, unless approved by the governor within thirty days after such adjournment
the appropriation so objected to shall not take effect

a4-s8.plain: A rule or regulation of a state department, board, bureau, officer, authority or commission, other than one on organization or internal management, is not effective until filed in the office of the department of state. The legislature must provide for its speedy publication.
limits: shall be effective until it is filed in the office of the department of state

a5-s1.plain: The comptroller and attorney-general are chosen at the same election as the governor for the same term. The comptroller must audit vouchers, accounts and revenues; payment of state money without the comptroller's audit is void. The legislature may assign the comptroller only certain further duties.
rights: may be restrained upon the suit of any taxpayer
powers: may also assign to him or her
limits: No election of a comptroller or an attorney-general shall be had except at the time of electing a governor
shall be void
shall assign to him or her no administrative duties

a5-s2.plain: There may be no more than twenty civil departments in the state government, including those referred to in the constitution. The legislature may by law change the names of those departments.
powers: may by law change the names of the departments referred to in this constitution
limits: There shall be not more than twenty civil departments in the state government

a5-s3.plain: Subject to the constitution's limits, the legislature may by law assign new powers and functions to departments, officers, boards, commissions or executive offices of the governor, and increase, modify or diminish them. It may also create temporary commissions and executive offices of the governor and reduce the number of departments.
powers: may from time to time assign by law new powers and functions
increase, modify or diminish their powers and functions
creating temporary commissions for special purposes or executive offices of the governor
reducing the number of departments

a5-s4.plain: The comptroller heads audit and control, the attorney-general heads law, and the Regents head education and appoint a commissioner of education. Most other department heads and board and commission members are appointed by the governor with the senate's advice and consent, and may be removed by the governor.
powers: shall appoint and at pleasure remove a commissioner of education
shall be appointed by the governor by and with the advice and consent of the senate
may be removed by the governor

a5-s6.plain: Civil service appointments and promotions must be made by merit and fitness, ascertained where practicable by competitive examination. Qualifying war veterans receive additional examination credit, more if disabled in war, but generally only for one appointment or promotion.
rights: shall be entitled to receive five points additional credit
shall be entitled to receive ten points additional credit
limits: No such member shall receive the additional credit granted by this section after he or she has received one appointment

a5-s7.plain: After July 1, 1940, membership in a state or civil division pension or retirement system is a contractual relationship whose benefits may not be diminished or impaired. A public officer convicted of a felony directly related to the officer's duties may have the pension reduced or revoked by a court after notice and a hearing.
rights: membership in any pension or retirement system of the state or of a civil division thereof shall be a contractual relationship
powers: may be reduced or revoked
limits: shall not be diminished or impaired

a6-s1.plain: The state has a unified court system: the court of appeals, supreme court and appellate divisions, court of claims, county, surrogate's and family courts, New York City's city-wide courts, and local courts outside the city. Listed courts are courts of record, and their process may be served across the state.
powers: may upon the request of the mayor and the local legislative body of the city of New York, merge the two courts
The legislature may provide that processes, warrants and other mandates of the district court may be served and executed in any part of the state

a6-s2.plain: The court of appeals has a chief judge and six associate judges serving fourteen-year terms; supreme court justices may be designated to serve temporarily. Vacancies are filled by the governor, with the senate's advice and consent, from persons recommended by a commission on judicial nomination.
powers: the court may designate any justice of the supreme court to serve as associate judge
The court shall have power to appoint and to remove its clerk
the governor shall designate such number of justices of the supreme court
The governor may fill vacancies among such designated judges
The governor shall appoint, with the advice and consent of the senate
the governor shall fill the vacancy by interim appointment
limits: no more than seven judges shall sit in any case
The powers and jurisdiction of the court shall not be suspended for want of appointment
No member of the commission shall hold any office in any political party
no person may be appointed a judge of the court of appeals unless such person is a resident of the state

a6-s3.plain: The court of appeals reviews only questions of law, except in death judgments or where the appellate division finds new facts. Appeals may be taken in criminal cases as provided and in listed classes of civil cases, some as of right. The court must adopt a rule to answer certified questions of New York law.
rights: the right to appeal shall not depend upon the amount involved
powers: The legislature may abolish an appeal to the court of appeals as of right
shall adopt and from time to time may amend a rule to permit the court to answer questions of New York law
limits: The jurisdiction of the court of appeals shall be limited to the review of questions of law
No appeal shall be taken to the court of appeals

a6-s4.plain: The state is divided into four judicial departments. The governor designates the justices of each appellate division, which has seven or five justices; additional or temporary justices may be designated, and appeals may be transferred between departments. Appellate divisions keep their existing jurisdiction plus any added by law.
powers: Once every ten years the legislature may alter the boundaries of the judicial departments
The governor shall designate the presiding justice of each appellate division
the governor may designate an additional justice or additional justices
may transfer any pending appeals from such department to any other department
Each appellate division shall have power to appoint and remove its clerk
limits: but without changing the number thereof
No more than five justices shall sit in any case
exercise any of the powers of a justice of the supreme court

a6-s5.plain: An appellate court authorized to review a judgment or order may reverse, affirm or modify it, wholly or in part, and must then render judgment according to law, or grant a new trial or hearing where necessary or proper. An appeal taken to an unauthorized appellate court must be transferred to an authorized one.
powers: may reverse or affirm, wholly or in part, or may modify the judgment or order appealed from
may grant a new trial or hearing

a6-s6.plain: The state has eleven judicial districts, each made of listed counties; once every ten years the legislature may change them. Supreme court justices are elected by district voters for fourteen-year terms. The legislature may increase or decrease the number of justices within limits, and county clerks are clerks of the supreme court.
powers: Once every ten years the legislature may increase or decrease the number of judicial districts or alter the composition of judicial districts
The legislature may increase the number of justices of the supreme court in any judicial district
The legislature may decrease the number of justices of the supreme court in any judicial district
limits: shall not be increased to exceed one justice for fifty thousand, or fraction over thirty thousand, of the population thereof
shall not be less than the number of justices of the supreme court authorized by law on the effective date of this article

a6-s7.plain: The supreme court has general original jurisdiction in law and equity and the appellate jurisdiction provided. In New York City it has exclusive jurisdiction over crimes prosecuted by indictment, though the legislature may give some to other city courts. It also has jurisdiction over new classes of actions the legislature creates.
powers: The supreme court shall have general original jurisdiction in law and equity
it shall have exclusive jurisdiction over crimes prosecuted by indictment
the supreme court shall have jurisdiction over such classes of actions and proceedings

a6-s8.plain: Each appellate division may establish appellate terms of three to five supreme court justices, designated by the chief administrator of the courts with the presiding justice's approval. No more than three sit in a case; two are a quorum and must concur. Appellate terms hear certain appeals as directed or provided by law.
powers: may establish an appellate term
shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine appeals from the district court or a town, village or city court outside the city of New York
limits: no more than three justices assigned thereto shall sit in any action or proceeding

a6-s9.plain: The court of claims has eight judges, a number the legislature may increase or reduce to six or seven. Judges are appointed by the governor with the senate's advice and consent for nine-year terms. The court hears claims against the state, by the state, or between conflicting claimants as the legislature provides.
powers: the legislature may increase such number and may reduce such number to six or seven
shall be appointed by the governor by and with the advice and consent of the senate
The court shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine claims against the state

a6-s10.plain: Each county outside New York City keeps a county court with at least one judge, plus any more provided by law. Its judges must be residents of the county, are chosen by the county's electors, and serve ten-year terms.

a6-s11.plain: The county court has jurisdiction over actions for money or chattels and certain liens up to twenty-five thousand dollars, all crimes and other violations of law, summary proceedings to recover real property, and others provided by law, plus equity and local appeals. This does not limit the supreme court's jurisdiction.
powers: The county court shall have jurisdiction over the following classes of actions and proceedings
shall exercise such equity jurisdiction as may be provided by law
shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine all appeals arising in the county
limits: shall in no way limit or impair the jurisdiction of the supreme court

a6-s12.plain: Each county keeps a surrogate's court with at least one judge, who must reside in the county and is elected by its electors, for fourteen years in New York City and ten elsewhere. It has jurisdiction over decedents' affairs, wills, estates, guardianship of minors' property and other matters provided by law.
powers: The surrogate's court shall have jurisdiction over all actions and proceedings relating to the affairs of decedents
The surrogate's court shall exercise such equity jurisdiction as may be provided by law
limits: shall in no way limit or impair the jurisdiction of the supreme court

a6-s13.plain: The family court is established, with judges appointed by the mayor in New York City and elected by county electors elsewhere, for ten-year terms. It has jurisdiction over listed matters, including neglected or delinquent minors, custody, adoption, support, paternity and conciliation of spouses, and certain matters referred from the supreme court.
powers: The family court shall have jurisdiction over the following classes of actions and proceedings
shall be appointed by the mayor of the city of New York for terms of ten years
The family court shall also have jurisdiction to determine, with the same powers possessed by the supreme court
limits: Nothing in this section shall be construed to abridge the authority or jurisdiction of courts to appoint guardians
shall in no way limit or impair the jurisdiction of the supreme court

a6-s14.plain: The legislature may provide that, outside the city of New York, the same person may act as county judge and surrogate, as family court judge and surrogate, as county judge and family court judge, or in all three positions in any county.
powers: may at any time provide that outside the city of New York the same person may act and discharge the duties

a6-s15.plain: The legislature must establish city-wide civil and criminal courts for New York City and may merge them on the city's request. Civil judges are elected and criminal judges appointed by the mayor, for ten-year terms. The section sets each court's jurisdiction without limiting the supreme court's.
powers: may, upon the request of the mayor and the local legislative body of the city of New York, merge the two courts
shall be appointed for terms of ten years by the mayor of the city of New York
shall have jurisdiction over the following classes of actions and proceedings
shall have jurisdiction over crimes and other violations of law
limits: shall in no way limit or impair the jurisdiction of the supreme court

a6-s16.plain: The Nassau county district court may continue, and the legislature may, on a county's request, establish a district court for all or part of a county outside New York City, subject to approval at a general election. Its jurisdiction, districts, judges and six-year terms are set out.
powers: may, at the request of the board of supervisors or other elective governing body of any county outside the city of New York, establish the district court
may create districts of the district court
may regulate and discontinue the district court
limits: No law establishing the district court for an entire county shall become effective unless approved at a general election
No law establishing the district court for a portion of a county shall become effective unless approved at a general election
but not in any respect greater than the jurisdiction of the courts for the city of New York
shall not exceed fifteen thousand dollars exclusive of interest and costs

a6-s17.plain: Town, village and city courts outside New York City continue, with jurisdiction set by the legislature but no greater than the district court's. The legislature may regulate them and discontinue village or city courts; a town court only with voter approval. Town justices are elected for four-year terms.
powers: may regulate such courts
may discontinue any village or city court outside the city of New York
may abolish the legislative functions on town boards of justices of the peace
limits: but not in any respect greater than the jurisdiction of the district court
only with the approval of a majority of the total votes cast at a general election

a6-s18.plain: Trial by jury is guaranteed as provided in article one. The legislature may set juries of six or twelve and allow trial without a jury for crimes not prosecuted by indictment, but crimes prosecuted by indictment are tried by twelve jurors unless jury trial is waived.
rights: Trial by jury is guaranteed
crimes prosecuted by indictment shall be tried by a jury composed of twelve persons
powers: may provide that in any court of original jurisdiction a jury shall be composed of six or of twelve persons
to try such matters without a jury
may provide for the manner of trial of actions and proceedings involving claims against the state

a6-s19.plain: The section sets when courts may or must transfer actions and proceedings to other courts: each court must send on cases outside its jurisdiction, and the supreme court and others may transfer cases to courts with jurisdiction. Each court must exercise jurisdiction over cases transferred to it.
powers: The supreme court may transfer any action or proceeding
the supreme court may transfer to itself any action or proceeding
The county court may transfer any action or proceeding
the supreme court or the county court may transfer to the county court any action or proceeding
may provide that the verdict or judgment in actions and proceedings so transferred shall not be subject to the limitation of monetary jurisdiction

a6-s20.plain: Judges of the higher courts must have been admitted to practice law in New York for ten years, and judges of other listed courts for five. Judges of the listed courts may not hold other public office, run for non-judicial office without resigning, hold political party office, or practice law.
powers: the legislature may enact such legislation as it deems appropriate to provide for a temporary judge or justice
shall be prescribed by the legislature
limits: unless he or she has been admitted to practice law in this state at least ten years
unless he or she has been admitted to practice law in this state at least five years
hold any other public office or trust
be eligible to be a candidate for any public office other than judicial office
hold any office or assume the duties or exercise the powers of any office of any political organization
engage in the practice of law, act as an arbitrator, referee or compensated mediator

a6-s21.plain: A vacancy, other than by expiration of term, in an elected judgeship is filled for a full term at the next general election at least three months later, with an interim appointment until then. A court of claims vacancy is filled like an original appointment; appointed New York City judgeships are filled by the mayor.
powers: the governor may fill such vacancy by an appointment
the mayor of the city of New York may fill such vacancy by an appointment
the mayor of the city of New York shall fill such vacancy by an appointment for the unexpired term
such county executive officer may, subject to confirmation by the board of supervisors

a6-s22.plain: A commission on judicial conduct hears complaints about judges and may determine that a judge be admonished, censured, removed or retired, subject to review by the court of appeals. The section sets the commission's eleven members and terms, and lets the court of appeals suspend judges.
rights: may either accept the commission's determination or make written request to the chief judge
shall receive his or her judicial salary during such period of suspension
powers: shall receive, initiate, investigate and hear complaints
may determine that a judge or justice be admonished, censured or removed from office for cause
may establish its own rules and procedures not inconsistent with law
the court of appeals may admonish, censure, remove or retire
The court of appeals may suspend a judge or justice from exercising the powers of his or her office
the court of appeals may suspend a judge or justice from office
the legislature may provide by law for review of determinations of the commission on judicial conduct
limits: shall be ineligible to hold other judicial office

a6-s23.plain: Judges of the court of appeals and supreme court justices may be removed by a two-thirds vote of both houses; judges of other listed courts by a two-thirds senate vote on the governor's recommendation. Removal requires cause entered on the journals, a statement of the cause, and an opportunity to be heard.
rights: shall have had an opportunity to be heard
powers: may be removed by concurrent resolution of both houses of the legislature
may be removed by the senate, on the recommendation of the governor
limits: No judge or justice shall be removed by virtue of this section except for cause

a6-s24.plain: The assembly may impeach by a majority of all members elected. The senate president, senators and court of appeals judges try impeachments; conviction needs two-thirds of members present. Judgment extends only to removal and disqualification, but the party impeached remains liable to indictment and punishment.
powers: The assembly shall have the power of impeachment
limits: neither the lieutenant-governor nor the temporary president of the senate shall act as a member of the court
No judicial officer shall exercise his or her office
no person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of the members present
Judgment in cases of impeachment shall not extend further than to removal from office

a6-s25.plain: Compensation of the listed judges is set by law and may not be diminished during their term. These judges retire at the end of the year they turn seventy, but former court of appeals judges and supreme court justices may, if certified, serve as supreme court justices until seventy-six.
rights: shall receive without interruption or diminution
powers: may thereafter perform the duties of a justice of the supreme court, with power to hear and determine actions and proceedings
shall be eligible for designation by the governor as a temporary or additional justice of the appellate division
limits: shall not be diminished during the term of office for which he or she was elected or appointed
shall serve no longer than until the last day of December in the year in which he or she reaches the age of seventy-six

a6-s26.plain: Judges and justices of the listed courts may perform their duties or hold court in any county and may be temporarily assigned to the courts named. The chief administrator of the courts makes the assignments, and an assigned judge has the powers of the court to which assigned.
powers: A justice of the supreme court may perform the duties of office or hold court in any county
may be temporarily assigned to the supreme court in any judicial district or to the court of claims
shall be made by the chief administrator of the courts
may provide for temporary assignments within the county of residence or any adjoining county
also may be temporarily assigned by the chief administrator of the courts
shall have the powers, duties and jurisdiction of a judge or justice of the court to which assigned

a6-s27.plain: The governor may appoint extraordinary terms of the supreme court when in the governor's opinion the public interest requires, designating the time, place and justice. The governor may end the justice's assignment and name another justice.
powers: may, when in his or her opinion the public interest requires, appoint extraordinary terms of the supreme court
may terminate the assignment of the justice

a6-s28.plain: The chief judge of the court of appeals is the chief judge of the state and heads the unified court system, with an administrative board of the courts. The chief judge appoints a chief administrator, who supervises the court system, and sets standards and policies approved by the court of appeals.
powers: appoint a chief administrator of the courts who shall serve at the pleasure of the chief judge
shall supervise the administration and operation of the unified court system
shall establish standards and administrative policies for general application throughout the state

a6-s29.plain: The legislature must provide for allocating the cost of running the listed courts among the state, counties, New York City and other subdivisions, and for submitting court budget estimates. The legislature and governor, or the local governing bodies, make the final determination for the expenses each bears.
powers: shall be made by the legislature and the governor
shall be made by the appropriate governing bodies

a6-s30.plain: The legislature keeps its power to alter and regulate court jurisdiction and proceedings, and may delegate its power over practice and procedure to a court or the chief administrator of the courts. Individual courts may still adopt regulations consistent with general practice and procedure.
powers: shall have the same power to alter and regulate the jurisdiction and proceedings in law and in equity
delegate, in whole or in part, to a court

a6-s31.plain: Article VI does not apply to the peacemakers courts or other Indian courts, which continue to exist and operate as provided by law.
limits: This article does not apply to the peacemakers courts or other Indian courts

a6-s32.plain: When a court commits, remands or places a child in its jurisdiction with an institution, agency or person, the child must be placed, when practicable, with an institution or agency governed by persons, or a person, of the same religious persuasion as the child.
rights: of the same religious persuasion as the child

a6-s33.plain: Existing laws not inconsistent with this article stay in force until changed under it. The legislature must enact laws to carry out the article and may enact other laws, not inconsistent with it, to implement, supplement or clarify its provisions.
powers: may, for the purpose of implementing, supplementing or clarifying any of its provisions, enact any laws

a6-s34.plain: Courts must decide the appeals, actions and proceedings pending in them when this article takes effect, with set exceptions for certain pending appeals. Justices and judges then in office keep their offices until their terms expire.

a6-s35.plain: Abolishes the children's courts and several New York City and county courts and the offices of special county judge, special surrogate and official referee, and moves their judges, staff, records and pending cases to the supreme court, the new city-wide courts or the family court. It sets how pending appeals are taken.
powers: shall provide by law that the justices of the city court of the city of New York
shall provide by law that the justices of the court of special sessions
may transfer any such appeal to an appellate term
may require the transfer of any such appeal to an appellate term
limits: shall not create a vacancy until the reduced number of personnel has been reached

a6-s36.plain: No civil or criminal appeal, action or proceeding pending when this article takes effect abates; each continues in the courts as this article provides, and later proceedings follow the laws then in force until superseded.
limits: No civil or criminal appeal, action or proceeding pending before any court or any judge or justice on the effective date of this article shall abate

a6-s36-a.plain: The 1976 amendments to articles six and seven become part of the constitution on the January 1 after the people approve them, but take effect the following April 1. Court of appeals judges then in office serve out their terms; vacancies are filled under section two of article six.

a6-s36-c.plain: The 1974 amendments to section twenty-two of article six become part of the constitution on the January 1 after the people approve them, but do not become operative until the following September 1, the effective date of the amendments.

a6-s37.plain: This article becomes part of the constitution on the January 1 after the people approve it, but its provisions do not become operative until the following September 1, which is its effective date.

a7-s1.plain: Department heads, except the legislature and judiciary, must give the governor budget estimates and information, and the governor holds hearings on them. The legislature's and judiciary's itemized estimates go to the governor by December 1 for inclusion in the budget without revision.
rights: shall be entitled to attend the hearings thereon and to make inquiry concerning any part thereof
powers: may require the attendance of heads of departments and their subordinates
limits: for inclusion in the budget without revision

a7-s2.plain: Each year, by a set date, the governor must submit to the legislature a budget with a complete plan of proposed expenditures and estimated available moneys and revenues, an explanation of the estimates, and recommended legislation.

a7-s3.plain: With the budget, the governor must submit bills containing all proposed appropriations and recommended legislation, and may amend or supplement it within thirty days, or later with the legislature's consent. The governor and department heads may appear and be heard on the budget, and department heads must when requested.
rights: shall have the right
powers: amend or supplement the budget and submit amendments to any bills submitted by him or her or submit supplemental bills

a7-s4.plain: The legislature may not alter the governor's appropriation bills except to strike out or reduce items, but may add separately stated items. Once passed by both houses, such a bill becomes law without the governor, except legislative and judiciary appropriations and added items, which need the governor's approval.
powers: it may add thereto items of appropriation
limits: may not alter an appropriation bill submitted by the governor except to strike out or reduce items therein

a7-s5.plain: Neither house may consider any other appropriation bill until both houses have finally acted on all the governor's appropriation bills, unless the governor certifies that immediate passage is necessary.
limits: Neither house of the legislature shall consider any other bill making an appropriation

a7-s6.plain: Apart from the governor's bills and a supplemental bill for the support of government, appropriations must be made by separate bills each for a single object or purpose. Provisions in the governor's appropriation bills must relate specifically to a particular appropriation.
limits: no appropriations shall be made except by separate bills each for a single object or purpose

No provision shall be embraced in any appropriation bill submitted by the governor or in such supplemental appropriation bill unless it relates specifically to some particular appropriation in the bill

a7-s7.plain: No money may be paid out of the state treasury or its funds except under an appropriation by law, and only within two years after the appropriation act passes. Each appropriation law must specify the sum and its object or purpose.
limits: No money shall ever be paid out of the state treasury or any of its funds, or any of the funds under its management, except in pursuance of an appropriation by law
it shall not be sufficient for such law to refer to any other law to fix such sum

a7-s8.plain: The state's money may not be given or loaned to private corporations, associations or undertakings, nor its credit to any individual or corporation, except for funds held for educational or mental health purposes. The legislature may still provide aid to the needy and others listed, and authorize loans to a public corporation to finance business facilities.
powers: providing for the aid, care and support of the needy
authorizing the loan of the money of the state to a public corporation
limits: The money of the state shall not be given or loaned to or in aid of any private corporation or association, or private undertaking
nor shall the credit of the state be given or loaned to or in aid of any individual, or public or private corporation or association, or private undertaking
shall not exceed sixty per centum of the cost of any such project
shall not exceed eighty per centum of the cost of any such project

a7-s9.plain: The state may borrow in anticipation of taxes and revenues within appropriations, repaying within one year, and in anticipation of proceeds of authorized bonds, repaying within two years, or five years for bonds for article eighteen purposes.
powers: The state may contract debts in anticipation of the receipt of taxes and revenues
The state may also contract debts in anticipation of the receipt of the proceeds of the sale of bonds theretofore authorized

a7-s10.plain: The state may also borrow to repel invasion, suppress insurrection, defend the state in war or suppress forest fires, but the money must be used only for that purpose or to repay the debts.
powers: the state may contract debts to repel invasion, suppress insurrection, or defend the state in war, or to suppress forest fires
limits: and to no other purpose whatever

a7-s11.plain: Apart from debts under sections 9, 10 and 13, state debt must be authorized by law for a single specified work or purpose and approved by a majority of voters at a general election. The legislature may repeal such a law before any debt is contracted, or forbid further debt under it.
powers: repeal the same
forbid the contracting of any further debt or liability under such law
limits: no debt shall be hereafter contracted by or in behalf of the state, unless such debt shall be authorized by law, for some single work or purpose
No such law shall take effect until it shall, at a general election, have been submitted to the people

a7-s12.plain: Apart from debts under sections 9, 10 and 13, state debts must follow set rules: principal paid in installments or through sinking funds, first payment within one year and last within forty years, no term beyond the probable life of the work, proceeds used only for the stated purpose, and sinking funds managed by the comptroller.
limits: No such debt shall be contracted for a period longer than that of the probable life of the work or purpose
shall be applied only to the work or purpose specified in the act authorizing such debt or liability
shall be used solely for the purpose of retiring the obligations secured thereby

a7-s13.plain: The legislature may provide for refunding state debts when the refunding achieves a present-value debt service savings. Refunding obligations may not exceed what the refunding needs, proceeds go into escrow funds managed by the comptroller, and installments, maturities and sinking funds follow set rules.
powers: may provide means and authority whereby any state debt or debts, or any portion or combination thereof, may be refunded
may provide for the method of computation of present value for such purpose
limits: no maturity shall be called for redemption unless the privilege to pay prior to the maturity date was reserved to the state
In no event shall refunding obligations be issued in an amount exceeding that necessary
shall the proceeds of refunding obligations be applied to any purpose other than accomplishing the refunding of the debt to be refunded and paying costs and expenses related to the refunding

a7-s14.plain: The legislature may authorize up to three hundred million dollars of state debt, without a vote of the people, to eliminate railroad grade crossings. The section sets how elimination costs are shared with railroad companies and municipalities, and lets up to sixty million dollars of bond proceeds go to state highways and parkways.
powers: may authorize by law the creation of a debt or debts of the state
shall be entitled to recover from the railroad company or companies
is hereby authorized to appropriate
limits: shall not exceed the difference between the amount of the debt or debts heretofore created or authorized by law
in no event to exceed fifteen per centum of the expense of the elimination
